subject: general
question: According to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index Report 2022, a total of 415 million people exited multidimensional poverty in India in the last ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**15 years**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **15 years** is the time period during which 415 million people exited multidimensional poverty in India according to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index Report 2022.
 
• The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is an international measure of acute poverty covering over 100 developing countries.
 
• The MPI identifies multiple deprivations at the household and individual levels in health, education, and standard of living.
 
• India has shown significant progress in reducing multidimensional poverty, reflecting improvements in various socio-economic indicators.
 
• This achievement is crucial for India's overall development and aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Global Multidimensional Poverty Index** was developed by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• The index complements traditional income-based poverty measures by considering multiple factors that contribute to poverty.
 
• India's reduction in multidimensional poverty is attributed to improved access to basic amenities, healthcare, education, and economic opportunities.
 
• The report highlights the importance of sustained policy efforts and targeted interventions to continue this positive trend.
 
• Addressing multidimensional poverty is essential for ensuring inclusive and equitable growth in India.
